title: Market velocity signal translation lab for LLM deployment readiness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a focused lab to translate external market and competitor signals (model availability, latency spikes, pricing moves, new variant releases) into actionable deployment-readiness indicators and automated fallback playbooks. Deliverables: (1) a normalized signal taxonomy mapped to our capacity + model-compatibility surface, (2) a small set of scorecards that drive canary/rollout triggers and dedicated procurement alerts, and (3) a prototype dashboard and alerting rules that feed into the Console and on-call runbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Signal taxonomy defined with at least 8 distinct signals and canonical source(s)
Scorecard computes a numeric readiness score for each region-model pair and is reproducible from stored telemetry
Two automated playbooks (canary fallback to model-variant, procurement alert) implemented as rule templates
Dashboard with trend view and alerting rules deployed to staging and tested with synthetic outages
Hand-off doc and 30-minute runbook readout with SRE and SalesOps completed
tasks: Inventory candidate external signal sources (third-party feeds, public model registries, telemetry anomalies)
Design normalization schema and enrichment steps (latency->severity buckets, price delta->cost-risk)
Prototype readiness score computation (Python notebook) and validate against historical incidents
Implement two rule templates in Console (canary fallback, procurement alert) and wire alert destinations
Build staging dashboard (Grafana/Console) and create synthetic-trigger test harness
Run cross-functional review with SRE/Eng/Support; capture follow-ups and owner assignment
Finalize PRD and migration notes; create follow-up Linear issues for scale work
notes: Motivation: customers experience surprise swaps when model variants are withdrawn or spikes in latency occur; business wants earlier, machine-readable indicators.
Trade-offs: aim for high precision on alerts initially to avoid alert fatigue; recall can be increased in follow-ups once labeling improves.
Data constraints: some third-party feeds are rate-limited and may have variable freshness; fallback playbooks must tolerate stale signals.
Stakeholders: Growth (pricing signals), SalesOps (procurement alerts), SRE (automation rules), Legal (third-party feed contracts)
